intro: Hi! At A1 you read menus, signs and very short messages. Now you read longer everyday texts: emails from a colleague or a hotel, messages from friends, short news stories and stories about someone's day. You'll also learn a useful trick: guessing a new word from the words around it.
teachingNotes: Reading at A2 means short real texts of 40–90 words: emails (from a colleague, a hotel, a shop), chat messages from friends, short news stories and stories about someone's day. Keep the A1 habit: read the question first, decide what the answer looks like (a name, a time, a place, a number, yes/no), scan for it, then read that sentence and the ones around it carefully. Answers are short and come from the text alone; never test general knowledge.

Emails and messages: From / To / Subject come first; Subject = perihal (the topic), not the grammar 'subject'. The name at the end is the writer: I = the writer, you = the reader, we = the writer's group (in a hotel email, we = the hotel). 'Dear Mr Pratama' is the normal polite opening (like 'Yth.'), not romantic 'sayang'. Watch for changed plans ('not on Tuesday now', 'Room 5, not Room 2'): learners grab the first day or room they see. Teach fixed phrases as chunks: Please…, Can you…? (asking for help), Thanks for…, Sorry about…, Let me know, See you…, Best wishes / Regards.

Stories and news: the headline (judul berita) gives the topic; the text answers who, what, where, when and why. Events are in the past simple, which the learner knows: regular -ed (started, walked, cleaned) and the core irregular list (went, had, got, saw, ate, bought, made, came, took, said, did, drank). Indonesian never changes the verb (Kemarin dia pergi), so learners may not recognise went or bought as forms of go and buy: help them link the past form to the base verb. A common mix-up: bought (buy, membeli) vs brought (bring, membawa). The order of events comes from time phrases (last Sunday, at 6 am, in the afternoon) and first, then, after that.

The biggest reading trap: a wrong option that uses the same words as the text but says something different (the text says the pool is open from 7 am to 9 pm; the option says 'the pool opens at 9 pm'). Teach learners to compare the whole sentence, not single words. For Did…? questions, answer from the text, not from what seems likely: someone who wanted to or started to do something may not have done it (She wanted to buy a phone, but the shop was closed → Did she buy a phone? No).

Guessing from context: 1) Is the new word a thing, an action or a description? 2) Read the words before and after it and the next sentence: they often explain it. 3) Use the small clue words the learner knows: and (similar idea), but (opposite), so / because (result, reason). 4) Try the guess in the sentence. 5) Only guess words needed for the question; skip the rest. Accept an Indonesian meaning or a simple English synonym (exhausted = sangat lelah / very tired). Don't translate phrases word by word.

Limits: texts use only A0/A1 grammar plus the past simple (regular, irregular, did questions and negatives). No present perfect, no will, no going to: emails about the future use the present simple (Check-in is from 2 pm, The meeting is on Thursday) or set phrases (See you on Friday, I'd like to…). No could, have to or must. Keep texts to 40–90 words with Indonesian contexts (hotels in Yogyakarta or Lombok, the office, warung, ojek, power cuts). If a learner meets another irregular verb, just give its base form as a word to remember.

keyPoints.title: Emails and messages
keyPoints.explanation: Look at From, To and Subject first: they tell you who writes, to whom, and what it's about. The name at the end is the writer, so I = the writer and you = the reader; in an email from a hotel, we = the hotel. Read the question, find the sentence with the answer and read all of it: messages often change a plan (not Monday now, Wednesday).

examples.en: Dear Ms Sari, thank you for your email.
examples.id: Yth. Ibu Sari, terima kasih atas email Anda.

examples.en: Can you call me after 3? Thanks! – Budi
examples.id: Bisa telepon aku setelah jam 3? Makasih! – Budi

id.title: Email dan pesan
id.explanation: Lihat From, To dan Subject dulu: dari situ kamu tahu siapa yang menulis, untuk siapa, dan tentang apa. Nama di akhir adalah penulisnya, jadi I = penulis dan you = pembaca; di email dari hotel, we = pihak hotel. Baca pertanyaannya, temukan kalimat yang berisi jawabannya, lalu baca kalimat itu sampai habis: pesan sering mengubah rencana (not Monday now, Wednesday = bukan Senin lagi, tapi Rabu).

keyPoints.title: Stories and short news
keyPoints.explanation: The headline gives the topic. The text tells you who, what, where, when and why. Stories happened in the past, so the verbs are in the past simple: -ed (started, cleaned) or an irregular form (went = go, bought = buy, saw = see). Time words like last Sunday, at 6 am, then and in the evening show the order of events.

examples.en: Last Sunday a new café opened in Malang.
examples.id: Minggu lalu sebuah kafe baru dibuka di Malang.

examples.en: At 8 she took the bus to the market and bought some fish.
examples.id: Jam 8 dia naik bus ke pasar dan membeli ikan.

examples.en: In the evening they went home.

id.title: Cerita dan berita pendek
id.explanation: Headline (judul berita) memberi tahu topiknya. Isi teksnya menjawab siapa, apa, di mana, kapan dan kenapa. Cerita terjadi di masa lalu, jadi kata kerjanya dalam bentuk lampau (past simple): +ed (started, cleaned) atau bentuk tidak beraturan (went = go, bought = buy, saw = see). Kata waktu seperti last Sunday, at 6 am, then dan in the evening menunjukkan urutan kejadiannya.

keyPoints.title: Guessing new words
keyPoints.explanation: Don't stop at every new word. When you need one, ask: is it a thing, an action or a description? Then read the words around it and the next sentence: they often explain it. Clue words help: and = a similar idea, but = the opposite, so / because = a result / a reason. Try your guess in the sentence: does it make sense?

examples.en: The bakery near my house sells fresh bread and cakes.
I worked for 12 hours. I was exhausted, so I went to bed at 8.
examples.id: exhausted = sangat lelah (petunjuk: 12 jam kerja, so, tidur)

examples.en: The room was tiny, but the bed was big.
examples.id: tiny = sangat kecil (petunjuk: but = kebalikan dari big)

id.title: Menebak arti kata baru
id.explanation: Jangan berhenti di setiap kata baru. Kalau kamu memerlukan satu kata, tanyakan: apakah ini benda, kegiatan, atau sifat (keadaan sesuatu)? Lalu baca kata-kata di sekitarnya dan kalimat berikutnya: sering kali di situ ada penjelasannya. Kata kecil bisa jadi petunjuk: and = ide yang mirip, but = kebalikannya, so / because = akibat / alasan. Coba masukkan tebakanmu ke kalimatnya: masuk akal tidak?

guidedPractice.prompt: Read the message from Pak Hasan: 'Hi Rina, the printer on the 3rd floor is broken. Please use the printer in Room 8 on the 5th floor. The paper is in the cupboard next to the door. And please don't print in colour: it's very expensive. Thanks! Pak Hasan'. Where can Rina print today? Write the room.
guidedPractice.hint: The 3rd-floor printer is broken. Look for the sentence that starts with 'Please use…'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read the message: 'Hi Mr Wijaya, your order from Toko Sepatu Rapi is on the way. Our courier, Agus, comes to your house between 1 and 3 pm today. Please keep your phone on. Nobody at home? He can leave the box with your neighbour. Thanks! Toko Sepatu Rapi'. Who is Agus?
guidedPractice.hint: Look at the words just before the name: 'Our courier, Agus'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read the story: 'Yesterday was a bad day for Budi. He got up late and missed the 7 o'clock bus. He took an ojek, but there was a lot of traffic on Jalan Sudirman. He arrived at the office at 8:40, forty minutes late. At lunch he ate nasi goreng at his desk because he had a lot of work.' What time did Budi arrive at the office?
guidedPractice.hint: Look for the word 'arrived' and the time after it. 7 o'clock is the bus he missed.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read: 'My grandmother is 80, but she is very fit. She walks for an hour every morning, she does yoga on Fridays and she cleans her big house without help. She is never ill, and she can carry heavy bags from the market.' What does 'fit' mean here? Write it in Indonesian or in simple English.
guidedPractice.hint: What does she do every morning? And 'but' after '80' shows something surprising for an old person.

independentPractice.prompt: Read the news: 'NEW NIGHT MARKET IN MALANG · Last Friday a new night market opened next to the train station in Malang. It has 60 food stalls and a small stage for music. On the first night more than 5,000 people came. The market is open from 5 pm to 11 pm, Thursday to Sunday.' How many food stalls does the market have?
independentPractice.hint: Scan for the number next to 'food stalls'. 5,000 is the number of people.

independentPractice.prompt: Read: 'Yesterday I had lunch at the new warung near my office. The rice and the tempe were good, but the chicken soup was very bland, so I added salt, pepper and some chilli. With the salt and chilli, it was delicious!' What does 'bland' mean? Write it in Indonesian or in simple English.
independentPractice.hint: Why did the writer add salt and chilli? What was wrong with the soup before?

independentPractice.prompt: Read the email: 'Subject: Saturday class · Hi everyone, there is no English class this Saturday because our teacher, Ms Dewi, is sick. The next class is on Saturday 14 June at 9 am, in Room 4 as usual. Best wishes, Andi (class secretary)'. Is there a class this Saturday? Write yes or no.
independentPractice.hint: Read the first sentence of the message to the end: 'there is no English class…'.

assessment.prompt: Read the email: 'From: Hotel Melati, Yogyakarta · To: Dimas Pratama · Subject: Your booking · Dear Mr Pratama, thank you for your booking for 3–5 August. Your room is on the third floor. Check-in is from 2 pm and check-out is at 12 noon. Breakfast is in the garden restaurant from 6 to 10 am. Please bring your ID card. Best wishes, Ayu, Reception'. What time is check-out?
assessment.rubric: Correct: 12 noon (also 12, 12:00, 12 pm, noon, midday, jam 12 siang). '2 pm' (that's check-in) = 0. '10 am' (end of breakfast) = 0.

assessment.prompt: Read Budi's email: 'Subject: Meeting with Maju Jaya · Hi Rina, the clients from Maju Jaya called this morning. The meeting isn't on Tuesday now: it's on Thursday at 10 am, and it's in Room 5, not Room 2. Can you print the price list for them? I'm at the bank until 11, so please call me after that. Thanks! Budi'. Which room is the meeting in?
assessment.rubric: Correct: Room 5. 'Room 2' = 0 (the email says NOT Room 2). '10' or '11' (times) = 0.

assessment.prompt: Read Lina's message to Sari: 'Hi Sari, I'm so sorry about yesterday! On the way to your house my motorbike had a flat tyre. I pushed it to a garage near the market and waited there for two hours, so after that I went home. And my phone battery was dead! Are you free on Saturday? I'd like to take you to the new café near the station. Lina'. Did Lina arrive at Sari's house yesterday? Write yes or no.
assessment.rubric: Correct: no (she went to a garage and then went home). 'yes' = 0. 'tidak' (right idea, Indonesian) = 70.

assessment.prompt: Read the news story: 'FUN RUN FOR A CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL · Last Sunday more than 2,000 people joined a fun run in Bandung. The race started at Gedung Sate at 6 am and finished in Braga Street. The youngest runner was 7, and the oldest, Pak Ujang, was 81. He finished in 55 minutes! The money from the tickets went to a children's hospital in the city.' Where in Bandung did the race start?
acceptableAnswers: the race started at gedung sate
assessment.rubric: Correct: Gedung Sate. 'Braga Street' = 0 (that's where it finished). 'a children's hospital' = 0 (that's where the money went).

assessment.prompt: Read the story: 'A BUSY SATURDAY · On Saturday Dewi got up at 5 am and made nasi uduk for her family. At 8 she took the bus to Pasar Baru and bought vegetables, fish and flowers. At the market she saw her old friend Yanti, and they drank coffee together at a small warung. In the afternoon Dewi cleaned the house. In the evening she was very tired, but happy.' Who did Dewi see at the market? Write the name.
acceptableAnswers: she saw her old friend yanti
assessment.rubric: Correct: Yanti. 'her old friend' without the name = 70. 'her family' or any other answer = 0.

assessment.prompt: Read: 'Last night there was a power cut in our street. At 7 pm all the lights went off, the fan stopped and the TV went black. My neighbours came out of their houses with torches. The lights came back at 10 pm.' What does 'power cut' mean? Write it in Indonesian or in simple English.
assessment.rubric: Correct: mati listrik / pemadaman listrik / no electricity. 'pemotongan' or 'potongan' (word-by-word 'cut') = 0. 'the lights went off' alone = 70 (right clue, but the whole street had no electricity).

assessment.prompt: Read Andi's message: 'The train this morning was really crowded! There were people everywhere, and I stood for the whole trip. I didn't have space to open my bag or read my book. Tomorrow I'd like to take the 5 am train: it's usually quiet.' What does 'crowded' mean? Write it in Indonesian or in simple English.
assessment.rubric: Correct: penuh sesak / ramai / full of people. 'sepi' or 'quiet' = 0 (that's the opposite: the 5 am train). 'terlambat' or 'late' = 0.

material.title: How to read an everyday text

blocks.text:
At A1 you scanned short texts for one piece of information. Now the texts are longer (40–90 words), but the plan is the same:
- **Look** at the type of text: an email, a chat message, a news story? The title or the **Subject** tells you the topic.
- **Read the question first.** Decide what the answer looks like: a name, a time, a place, a number, yes or no.
- **Scan** for it: names and places start with a capital letter, times have **am / pm** or **:**.
- **Read that sentence carefully**, and the sentences before and after it.
You don't need to understand every word. Many words you don't know are not in the question at all.

id.text:
Di A1 kamu sudah melakukan scanning: mencari satu informasi di teks pendek. Sekarang teksnya lebih panjang (40–90 kata), tapi caranya sama:
- **Lihat** jenis teksnya: email, pesan chat, atau berita? Judul atau **Subject** (perihal) memberi tahu topiknya.
- **Baca pertanyaannya dulu.** Tentukan seperti apa bentuk jawabannya: nama, jam, tempat, angka, yes atau no.
- **Scan** (cari dengan cepat): nama orang dan tempat diawali huruf kapital, jam memakai **am / pm** atau **:**.
- **Baca kalimat itu dengan teliti**, juga kalimat sebelum dan sesudahnya.
Kamu tidak perlu mengerti setiap kata. Banyak kata yang tidak kamu tahu sama sekali tidak ada hubungannya dengan pertanyaan.

rows.note: look for a day, a date, am / pm
look for a place: in, at, Room, Street

id.note: cari tempat: in, at, Room, Street

rows.note: look for by bus, by ojek, took a taxi

id.note: cari by bus, by ojek, took a taxi

blocks.text: **The biggest trap:** a wrong answer often uses **the same words** as the text but says something different. The text says *The pool is open from 7 am to 9 pm*; a wrong option says *The pool opens at 9 pm*. Don't choose an answer just because you see the same words in it: check that the whole sentence means the same thing.

id.text: **Jebakan terbesar:** jawaban yang salah sering memakai **kata-kata yang sama** dengan teks, tapi artinya berbeda. Teksnya bilang *The pool is open from 7 am to 9 pm* (kolam renang buka jam 7 pagi sampai jam 9 malam); pilihan yang salah bilang *The pool opens at 9 pm* (kolam renang buka jam 9 malam). Jangan pilih jawaban hanya karena ada kata yang sama: cek apakah seluruh kalimatnya artinya sama.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'The library is open from 8 am to 4 pm, Monday to Saturday.' Which sentence is true?
options: The library is open on Saturday.
The library is open on Sunday.
blocks.explain: Monday to Saturday includes Saturday, so it's open on Saturday. It opens at 8 am (4 pm is when it closes), and Sunday isn't in the days.

id.prompt: Baca: 'The library is open from 8 am to 4 pm, Monday to Saturday.' Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: Monday to Saturday (Senin sampai Sabtu) termasuk hari Sabtu, jadi perpustakaannya buka hari Sabtu. Bukanya jam 8 pagi (jam 4 sore itu jam tutupnya), dan hari Minggu tidak termasuk.

blocks.text:
An email has three lines at the top: **From** (the writer), **To** (the reader) and **Subject** (what the email is about). Then comes a greeting (**Dear Ms Sari**, **Hi Budi**), the message, a polite end (**Best wishes**, **Regards**, **Thanks**) and the writer's name.

Who is who? **I** = the writer, the name at the end. **You** = the reader. In an email from a hotel, a shop or an office, **we** = the hotel, the shop or the office. Chat messages work the same way, but they are shorter and often drop small words: *At the station now* = I'm at the station now.

id.text:
Email punya tiga baris di bagian atas: **From** (dari: penulisnya), **To** (kepada: pembacanya) dan **Subject** (perihal: email ini tentang apa). Lalu ada salam pembuka (**Dear Ms Sari**, **Hi Budi**), isi pesannya, salam penutup yang sopan (**Best wishes**, **Regards**, **Thanks**) dan nama penulisnya.

Siapa itu siapa? **I** = penulisnya, yaitu nama di akhir. **You** = pembacanya. Di email dari hotel, toko atau kantor, **we** = pihak hotel, toko atau kantor itu. Pesan chat sama saja, tapi lebih pendek dan sering membuang kata-kata kecil: *At the station now* = I'm at the station now (aku sudah di stasiun).

rows.note: Please… = asks the reader to do something
a polite end; Regards means the same

id.note: penutup yang sopan; Regards artinya sama

blocks.text:
**Watch for changes.** Messages often change a plan: *The meeting isn't on Monday now: it's on Wednesday.* / *Room 4, not Room 6.* Many learners take the first day or room they see. Read the whole sentence and look for **not** and **now**.

**Subject** in an email means the topic (perihal). It isn't the 'subject' of a sentence. And **Dear** at the start of an email is just polite, like *Yth.*: you write it to your boss, a hotel or a stranger.

British and American: British English writes **Mr**, **Ms**, **Dr** with no full stop; American English writes **Mr.**, **Ms.**, **Dr.** Both are correct.

id.text:
**Perhatikan perubahan.** Pesan sering mengubah rencana: *The meeting isn't on Monday now: it's on Wednesday.* (rapatnya bukan hari Senin lagi, tapi Rabu) / *Room 4, not Room 6.* (Ruang 4, bukan Ruang 6). Banyak pelajar langsung mengambil hari atau ruangan pertama yang mereka lihat. Baca kalimatnya sampai habis dan cari kata **not** (bukan) dan **now** (sekarang).

**Subject** di email artinya perihal (topik). Ini bukan 'subjek' kalimat. Dan **Dear** di awal email hanya sopan santun, seperti *Yth.*: kamu menulisnya untuk atasan, hotel, atau orang yang belum kamu kenal. Artinya bukan 'sayang'.

Inggris dan Amerika: bahasa Inggris British menulis **Mr**, **Ms**, **Dr** tanpa titik; bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis **Mr.**, **Ms.**, **Dr.** Dua-duanya benar.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'Dear guests, we are sorry: the swimming pool is closed today for cleaning. Hotel Bunga, Malang'. Who is 'we'?
blocks.explain: The writer is at the end: Hotel Bunga. In an email or notice from a hotel, 'we' = the hotel. The guests are the readers ('Dear guests').

id.prompt: Baca: 'Dear guests, we are sorry: the swimming pool is closed today for cleaning. Hotel Bunga, Malang'. Siapa 'we' di sini?
id.explain: Penulisnya ada di akhir: Hotel Bunga. Di email atau pengumuman dari hotel, 'we' = pihak hotel. Para tamu (guests) adalah pembacanya ('Dear guests').

blocks.text:
A short news story starts with a **headline**, often in capital letters: *FREE CONCERT IN THE PARK*. Then the text answers **who, what, where, when** and **why**. A story about someone's day tells you what happened, in order.

Stories are about the past, so the verbs are in the **past simple**: regular verbs end in **-ed** (*started, cleaned, visited*), and irregular verbs change (*went, bought, saw*). Indonesian doesn't change the verb (*Kemarin dia **pergi** ke pasar*): in English the verb itself shows that it happened before. If you don't recognise a past form, think of its base form (the dictionary form): *went* → *go*.

id.text:
Berita pendek diawali **headline** (judul berita), sering dengan huruf kapital semua: *FREE CONCERT IN THE PARK* (konser gratis di taman). Lalu isinya menjawab **siapa, apa, di mana, kapan** dan **kenapa**. Cerita tentang hari seseorang memberi tahu apa yang terjadi, secara berurutan.

Cerita membahas masa lalu, jadi kata kerjanya (verb) dalam bentuk **past simple** (lampau): kata kerja beraturan diberi **-ed** (*started, cleaned, visited*), dan kata kerja tidak beraturan berubah bentuk (*went, bought, saw*). Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja (*Kemarin dia **pergi** ke pasar*): dalam bahasa Inggris, kata kerjanya sendiri yang menunjukkan bahwa kejadiannya sudah lewat. Kalau kamu tidak mengenali bentuk lampaunya, ingat bentuk dasarnya (bentuk di kamus): *went* → *go*.

blocks.text:
**Did…? questions about a story:** answer from the text, not from what seems normal. *Rina wanted to buy a new phone, but the shop was closed.* **Did Rina buy a phone?** **No.** She wanted to, but she didn't.

British and American: *centre* (UK) = *center* (US), *neighbour* (UK) = *neighbor* (US). Same words, different spelling.

id.text:
**Pertanyaan Did…? tentang cerita:** jawab berdasarkan teks, bukan berdasarkan apa yang biasanya terjadi. *Rina wanted to buy a new phone, but the shop was closed.* (Rina ingin membeli HP baru, tapi tokonya tutup.) **Did Rina buy a phone?** **No.** Dia ingin membeli, tapi tidak jadi.

Inggris dan Amerika: *centre* (UK) = *center* (US), *neighbour* (UK) = *neighbor* (US). Katanya sama, ejaannya beda.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'Yesterday Sari went to Mall Ciputra, saw a film and bought a new bag.' What does 'bought' mean?
blocks.explain: bought is the past of buy (membeli): Sari bought a bag = Sari membeli tas. Don't mix it up with brought, the past of bring (membawa).

id.prompt: Baca: 'Yesterday Sari went to Mall Ciputra, saw a film and bought a new bag.' Apa arti 'bought'?
id.explain: bought adalah bentuk lampau dari buy (membeli): Sari bought a bag = Sari membeli tas. Jangan tertukar dengan brought, bentuk lampau dari bring (membawa).

blocks.text:
Every real text has a few words you don't know. **Context** = the words and sentences around a word. Often they tell you what it means:
- Is the new word a **thing**, an **action** or a **description** (how something is)? After *a / the* it's usually a thing; after *was / is* it's often a description.
- Read the words **before and after** it, and the **next sentence**. They often explain it.
- Small words are clues: **and** = a similar idea, **but** = the opposite, **so** and **because** = a result or a reason.
- Put your guess in the sentence. Does it make sense?
Only guess the words you need for the question. Skip the rest.

id.text:
Setiap teks sungguhan punya beberapa kata yang tidak kamu tahu. **Konteks** = kata-kata dan kalimat di sekitar sebuah kata. Sering kali dari situ kamu bisa menebak artinya:
- Apakah kata baru itu **benda**, **kegiatan** (action), atau **sifat** (keadaan sesuatu)? Setelah *a / the* biasanya benda; setelah *was / is* sering sifat.
- Baca kata-kata **sebelum dan sesudahnya**, juga **kalimat berikutnya**. Sering kali di situ ada penjelasannya.
- Kata kecil adalah petunjuk: **and** = ide yang mirip, **but** = kebalikannya, **so** (jadi) dan **because** (karena) = akibat atau alasan.
- Masukkan tebakanmu ke kalimatnya. Masuk akal tidak?
Tebak hanya kata yang kamu perlukan untuk menjawab pertanyaan. Lewati yang lain.

rows.en: The bakery near my house sells fresh bread and cakes.
rows.id: Toko roti dekat rumahku menjual roti dan kue segar.
rows.note: bakery = a thing; clues: sells, bread, cakes

id.note: bakery = benda; petunjuk: sells, bread, cakes → toko roti

rows.en: I worked for 12 hours and didn't eat lunch. I was exhausted, so I went to bed at 8 pm.
rows.id: Aku bekerja 12 jam dan tidak makan siang. Aku sangat lelah, jadi aku tidur jam 8 malam.
rows.note: exhausted = a description; clues: 12 hours, no lunch, so, bed

id.note: exhausted = sifat; petunjuk: 12 jam, tidak makan siang, so, tidur → sangat lelah

rows.en: The hotel room was tiny, but the bed was big.
rows.id: Kamar hotelnya sangat kecil, tapi tempat tidurnya besar.
rows.note: tiny = the opposite of big (clue: but)

id.note: tiny = kebalikan dari big (petunjuk: but) → sangat kecil

blocks.text: Some words have two meanings, and the context tells you which one: *light* = **ringan** in *My bag is very light* and **lampu** in *The light in the kitchen is broken*. Don't translate a phrase word by word: first look at what happens in the text, then guess.

id.text: Ada kata yang punya dua arti, dan konteksnya yang memberi tahu arti yang mana: *light* = **ringan** di *My bag is very light* dan **lampu** di *The light in the kitchen is broken*. Jangan menerjemahkan frasa kata demi kata: lihat dulu apa yang terjadi di teks, baru tebak.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'The lift in our office was out of order, so we used the stairs to the 6th floor. My legs were tired!' What are 'stairs'?
blocks.explain: The lift was broken, so (result) they used the stairs to go up to the 6th floor, and their legs were tired: stairs = tangga. Another lift wouldn't make your legs tired.

id.prompt: Baca: 'The lift in our office was out of order, so we used the stairs to the 6th floor. My legs were tired!' Apa itu 'stairs'?
id.explain: Liftnya rusak, so (jadi, akibatnya) mereka memakai stairs untuk naik ke lantai 6, dan kaki mereka capek: stairs = tangga. Lift lain tidak akan membuat kaki capek.

id.title: Menebak arti kata baru dari konteks

suggestedQuestions: How can I understand an email if I don't know every word?
Who is 'we' in an email from a hotel?
How do I know what happened first in a story?
How can I guess what a new word means?

resources.title: An email from a friend
resources.note: Gregor emails his friend Samia to plan a visit and explains how to get to his flat. A2 level, with true/false tasks. A few sentences use will, going to and the present perfect (later lessons): you don't need them to answer.

id.note: Gregor mengirim email ke temannya, Samia, untuk merencanakan kunjungan dan menjelaskan jalan ke flat-nya. Level A2, dengan latihan benar/salah. Beberapa kalimat memakai will, going to dan present perfect (pelajaran berikutnya): kamu tidak memerlukannya untuk menjawab.

resources.title: An invitation to a job interview
resources.note: A formal email from a company: when and where the interview is, what to bring and how to check in. A2 level. It uses will for the future (a later lesson), but you can find the answers with what you know.

id.note: Email resmi dari sebuah perusahaan: kapan dan di mana wawancaranya, apa yang perlu dibawa, dan cara melapor saat datang. Level A2. Email ini memakai will untuk masa depan (pelajaran berikutnya), tapi kamu bisa menemukan jawabannya dengan yang sudah kamu tahu.

flashcards.front: went / bought / saw (di cerita) → bentuk dasarnya?
kata petunjuk untuk arti yang berlawanan

id.intro: Hai! Di A1 kamu sudah membaca menu, papan tanda dan pesan yang sangat pendek. Sekarang kamu membaca teks sehari-hari yang lebih panjang: email dari rekan kerja atau hotel, pesan dari teman, berita pendek dan cerita tentang hari seseorang. Kamu juga belajar trik yang berguna: menebak arti kata baru dari kata-kata di sekitarnya.
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara memahami email kalau aku tidak tahu semua katanya?
Bagaimana aku tahu apa yang terjadi duluan di sebuah cerita?
Bagaimana cara menebak arti kata baru?

assessment.rev-1: Baca email ini: 'From: Hotel Melati, Yogyakarta · To: Dimas Pratama · Subject: Your booking · Dear Mr Pratama, thank you for your booking for 3–5 August. Your room is on the third floor. Check-in is from 2 pm and check-out is at 12 noon. Breakfast is in the garden restaurant from 6 to 10 am. Please bring your ID card. Best wishes, Ayu, Reception'. Jam berapa check-out?
assessment.rev-2: Baca email dari Budi: 'Subject: Meeting with Maju Jaya · Hi Rina, the clients from Maju Jaya called this morning. The meeting isn't on Tuesday now: it's on Thursday at 10 am, and it's in Room 5, not Room 2. Can you print the price list for them? I'm at the bank until 11, so please call me after that. Thanks! Budi'. Rapatnya di ruang (room) berapa?
assessment.rev-3: Baca pesan Lina untuk Sari: 'Hi Sari, I'm so sorry about yesterday! On the way to your house my motorbike had a flat tyre. I pushed it to a garage near the market and waited there for two hours, so after that I went home. And my phone battery was dead! Are you free on Saturday? I'd like to take you to the new café near the station. Lina'. Apakah kemarin Lina sampai di rumah Sari? Tulis yes atau no.
assessment.rev-4: Baca berita ini: 'FUN RUN FOR A CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL · Last Sunday more than 2,000 people joined a fun run in Bandung. The race started at Gedung Sate at 6 am and finished in Braga Street. The youngest runner was 7, and the oldest, Pak Ujang, was 81. He finished in 55 minutes! The money from the tickets went to a children's hospital in the city.' Di mana di Bandung lomba larinya dimulai?
assessment.rev-5: Baca cerita ini: 'A BUSY SATURDAY · On Saturday Dewi got up at 5 am and made nasi uduk for her family. At 8 she took the bus to Pasar Baru and bought vegetables, fish and flowers. At the market she saw her old friend Yanti, and they drank coffee together at a small warung. In the afternoon Dewi cleaned the house. In the evening she was very tired, but happy.' Siapa yang Dewi temui di pasar? Tulis namanya.
assessment.rev-6: Baca: 'Last night there was a power cut in our street. At 7 pm all the lights went off, the fan stopped and the TV went black. My neighbours came out of their houses with torches. The lights came back at 10 pm.' Apa arti 'power cut'? Tulis dalam bahasa Indonesia atau dalam bahasa Inggris yang sederhana.
assessment.rev-7: Baca pesan dari Andi: 'The train this morning was really crowded! There were people everywhere, and I stood for the whole trip. I didn't have space to open my bag or read my book. Tomorrow I'd like to take the 5 am train: it's usually quiet.' Apa arti 'crowded'? Tulis dalam bahasa Indonesia atau dalam bahasa Inggris yang sederhana.
